Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted. On state-changing operations this status may also carry `code: csrf_token_invalid` (SR-041; see `CsrfTokenInvalid`). An enrolment-only session gets `code: mfa_enrollment_required` from every operation outside its allow-list (see the Enrolment-only session section of `info.description`). A session that holds a view-as context gets `code: view_as_read_only` from every state-changing operation outside the viewer's own ones, and `code: view_as_expired` from every operation outside them once the server has ended the context (see the View-as session section of `info.description`). Both honour the C-2.6 carve-out below: while viewing, the writes it names and engaging the kill switch on an account set are not refused (see the View-as session section), and leaving view-as is one call that nothing refuses. `detail` never echoes token or cookie values. On a dangerous operation it may carry `code: step_up_required`: that body is a step-up challenge for the refused request (`challenge_id`, `challenge_expires_at`, `action_class`, `action_summary`, `target` and, for `live_enablement` and `killswitch`, `step_up_reason`; see `POST /auth/step-up`, #2304). On an order submit or amend it may also be the order-entry gate's refusal: `code: trading_disabled` with a `reason` member (`TradingDisabledProblem`, #837 Q5). `reason` appears on gate refusals only: the B18 kill switch (FREEZE) and the live-not-enabled refusal are separate synchronous checks ahead of the gate, and they return `trading_disabled` without a `reason`. Like the gate, they run after authentication, RBAC and account-scope resolution, and the C-2.6 carve-out binds every synchronous refusal, not just the gate: attaching a missing native SL, tightening a stop or re-arming a protective trigger is never refused. A `trading_disabled` body without `reason` is this response's plain `Problem`, never a `TradingDisabledProblem` (whose `reason` is required), so a client tells the gate's refusal by that member. On `placeOrder` and `amendOrder` the three come after the idempotency lookup (see the order of the checks under Idempotency in `info.description`), so the exact repeat of an accepted request gets its stored outcome instead. On `placeOrder`, and on an `amendOrder` that increases exposure (#913 slice 4 ruling Q10), the `trading.oms_enabled` flag, while off, also refuses with `trading_disabled` and no `reason`, after the lookup and ahead of the three (#913 slice 3 ruling Q3), an admission that opens or increases exposure only: an order whose body says `reduce_only` passes it (21-database-schema.md section 10.7). On a live account's order mutation that `ArmToken` names (one that opens or increases exposure, `reversePosition`, or a leverage change) it may be `code: session_not_armed` (SR-043; see the `X-Arm-Token` parameter, `ArmToken`), decided after account scope like the gate, a synchronous refusal the carve-out binds too; `ArmToken` lists the carve-out's full set (24-internal-schemas.md section 8.10). `placeOrder`, `createTradeGroup`, `previewTradeGroup`, `cancelAllOrders`, `closeAllPositions`, `createTradeGroupDefinition` and `updateTradeGroupDefinition` refuse an exchange account named in their body that is outside the caller's grants, and one that does not exist, alike with `code: account_scope_denied` (see `AccountScopeDenied`). `createApiKey` and `testApiKey` answer `code: kek_unavailable` while the credential key (KEK) is unavailable (ADR-0009 Amendment 1). ProfileRejected.description:
A profile save that is refused, so nothing is stored (`validation_failed`). Each entry of
`errors` names the body member by its JSON path (`field`, such as
`sizing.risk_per_trade_pct` or `allowed_symbols[2]`) and the reason (`rule`); a refusal
against an exchange limit also names the instrument (`symbol`) and the limit (`limit`).

A body that fails its schema (a type, an enum, a pattern, a missing or unknown member) is
refused with those failures alone, each `rule` the validator's own type as on every route,
except two members named by rule: `native_stop_mandatory` (`require_native_stop` cannot
be set to `false`) and `stop_defines_r` (a stop in `r_multiple`: the stop defines R).
Then two passes run, each listing every failure it finds, the second only when the first
passes. The first needs no exchange data: `required` and `not_allowed` (the rules of
`AccountProfileInput`), `range` and `precision` (`limit` holds the bound broken, or the
decimal places allowed), `ladder_sum`, `above_leverage_cap`, `cap_unbounded` and
`default_has_own_operation`. `cap_unbounded` is a trading-enabled profile with a
loss-bounding cap left unbounded (`ap_trading_caps`, decision D11): any of the five bounds
`ProfileRiskCaps` requires. `default_has_own_operation` is a write that would move the
account's default (`is_default: true` on a create, or on a replace an `is_default` other
than the stored one); its `message` is "The default binding has its own operation."

The second checks the exchange's current limits for the account's environment, judged for
the entries the write introduces, from an instrument cache at most 15 minutes old
(refreshed first when older): `max_leverage`
(`leverage` above the maximum of a symbol the profile allows, which with `all_symbols` is
every listed one and for a pattern every one it matches, so a universal pattern such as
`*USDT` counts as `all_symbols`), `min_order_qty` and `qty_step` (`sizing.qty`),
`min_notional` (`risk_caps.max_position_notional_usd` below a symbol's minimum notional)
and `symbol_not_listed` (an entry that names no listed, trading linear USDT perpetual).
It reads that cache only when the write allows something new (an allow entry added or
changed, `all_symbols` set, a block entry removed) or moves a judged figure toward a limit
(`leverage` raised, `sizing.qty` changed, `risk_caps.max_position_notional_usd` lowered or
newly set), and then judges the entries the write introduces against every limit, and
every allowed symbol against a limit whose figure moved: a write that only narrows, or
saves the profile unchanged, reads no cache and is never refused for want of one.
`native_stop_mandatory`, `above_leverage_cap`, `cap_unbounded` and every refusal of the
second pass are audited as `profile.save_refused`.

`cap_unbounded` is audited though it arrives as a missing member: it is a cap removed
rather than raised (PF-T02), a refusal of the risk policy and not of shape. A body refused
only by rules of shape or by `default_has_own_operation` is not audited, semantic shape
such as `stop_defines_r` included.

AccountProfileInput.description:
A per-account profile as written; 24-internal-schemas.md section 9.2 maps each member to
its domain field and column. Values are in stored units: a percent is the percent shown
(`"0.5"` is 0.5 %), and a decimal holds at most the places of its column (18 for USDT
amounts, quantities and offsets, 6 for percents of equity and `stop_loss.fallback_pct`, 4
for `stop_loss.atr_multiple`, 2 for `leverage` and `risk_caps.max_leverage_cap`; 18 for a
rung's `qty_pct` and `r`), trailing zeros not counted, refused rather than rounded
(`precision`). Every USDT amount, quantity and offset, and a rung's `r`, is below 10^20 and
`stop_loss.atr_multiple` below 10^6, the bounds of their columns (`range`). A create and a
replace alike give a member they leave out its default, `null` where nullable (no cap),
never the stored value.

Beyond its schema the body must hold (`ProfileRejected` names each rule): the sizing
amount of `sizing.mode` and no other (`required`, `not_allowed`); a `stop_loss` when
`sizing.mode` is `risk_based` (`required`); no `allowed_symbols` with `all_symbols`
(`not_allowed`); every cap of `ProfileRiskCaps` bounded when `trading_enabled` is set
(`cap_unbounded`); `leverage` at most `risk_caps.max_leverage_cap`
(`above_leverage_cap`); and rungs that take at most the whole leg (`ladder_sum`).

params.description: Every parameter of the indicator, as stored when the preset was saved.

IndicatorPresetInput.description:
Writable preset fields, and the item of `WorkspaceBundle.indicator_presets`. `PUT` is a
full replacement: an omitted field takes its default. Only the server sets `id`,
`owner_user_id` (the caller), `is_builtin` (`false`), `created_at`, `updated_at` and
`deleted_at`: sent in a body, each is refused (`422`) like any other unknown property.
`name` is at most 80 characters as sent (rule `string_too_long`), then sanitised as
`WorkspaceInput.name` is; empty after sanitising is rule `string_too_short`, and a lone
surrogate is rule `invalid_unicode`.

indicator_code.description: An indicator `id` from `listIndicators`. A value outside the pattern is rule `invalid_indicator_code`, and one that names no catalogue indicator is `unknown_indicator`; neither message echoes the value. Immutable once saved.

is_favourite.description: Starred in the indicator picker. A built-in is starred by saving a copy of it (`createIndicatorPreset`), possible only once `listIndicators` lists the built-in's indicator.

name.description: At most 80 characters as sent, at least 1 after sanitising (above). Unique per owner and `indicator_code`, case-insensitive, among live presets (`409 conflict`, rule `name_taken`); a copy of a built-in may keep its name.

pane_target.description: Where the indicator draws: over the price pane, or in a sub-pane of its own.

params.description: The indicator's parameters, checked against its descriptor's `params_schema` (`listIndicators`) before anything is stored, and never clamped. Only the first parameter defect is reported: a key the descriptor does not declare (rule `additionalProperties` on `params`), else the first parameter, in the descriptor's order, that breaks one of its keywords (`type`, `enum`, `minimum`, `maximum` or `multipleOf` on `params.<name>`); the message names the bound, never the value. Stored complete and canonical: an omitted parameter is stored at its default, so changing a default later never alters a saved preset. At most 4 KiB, nesting depth 4 and 64 keys (rules `params_too_large`, `params_too_deep` and `params_too_many_keys`).

style.description: Optional; omitted means no style overrides (stored and returned as `{}`).

IndicatorPresetStyle.description:
Style overrides by design-token name: a closed set of keys, each taking a closed set of
token values from the E13-D04 token list (SR-E13-08), so no colour, CSS, URL or free text
is stored or handed to a renderer. A key or value outside the set is `422` rule
`style_not_allowed`, never dropped. The set is empty until E13-D04 publishes it, so only
`{}` is accepted today; its keys are then added here, additively (C-6.3).

Layout.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

updated_at.description: Concurrency token (also the `ETag`) of the whole layout aggregate, panes included: every write changes it, including a pane-only change and a default switch made by another layout. Always exactly 6 fractional digits plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`) and strictly increasing. Echo it exactly as received; never re-serialise it through a client date type.

slot.description: `slot_index` of a pane in the same layout.

LayoutGridPreset.description:
Named grid (`lay_preset`, `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1) or `custom`. A named preset stores
only its name and fixed cell proportions: `grid_spec` is `null`, and a pane's `slot_index`
is its cell in row-major reading order (a slot beyond the preset's cells is placed by the
client, e.g. floating). Any other arrangement, including a named grid whose divider was
dragged, is saved as `custom` with its tree in `grid_spec`. **Open-ended for readers.**

LayoutGridSpec.description:
Dock tree of a `custom` layout (`row` / `column` / `tabset` / `leaf`), checked at the API
boundary (`422`, field paths under `grid_spec`): depth at most 6 counting the root as 1
(rule `tree_too_deep`); at most 64 nodes and at most 16 leaves (rule `tree_too_large`);
every leaf names the `slot_index` of a pane in the same body (rule `unknown_slot`) and no
slot appears twice (rule `duplicate_leaf`), so the leaf cap also follows from `panes` having
at most 16 entries; a split's `sizes` has one entry per child (rule `sizes_mismatch`), each
in (0, 1], summing to 1 within 1e-6 (rule `sizes_sum`); a tabset's `active` indexes one of
its children (rule `active_out_of_range`). Panes that no leaf names are kept (floating or
minimised, placed by the client).

LayoutGridSplit.description: `row` lays children out left to right, `column` top to bottom; `sizes` are fractions of the container.

active.description: Index of the visible tab in `children`.

LayoutInput.description: Writable layout fields plus the complete pane set. `PUT` is a full replacement: an omitted field takes its default, an explicit `null` on a non-nullable field is refused, and the stored panes are replaced. Observable validation (depth, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `invalid_unicode`, `name` sanitising and rules) is as on `WorkspaceInput`.

crosshair_sync.description: Layout default for crosshair sync between panes of one sync group.

grid_spec.description: Required when `grid_preset` is `custom`, otherwise `null` or omitted.

hotkey_slot.description: `Ctrl+1..9` binding; unique among the workspace's live layouts (`409 conflict`, rule `hotkey_slot_taken`).

is_default.description: At most one live default per workspace; `true` clears the previous default in the same transaction.

name.description: At most 40 characters as sent, at least 1 after sanitising, as for workspace names. Unique per workspace, case-insensitive, among live layouts (`409 conflict`, rule `name_taken`).

panes.description: In any order: panes are keyed by `slot_index`, and responses sort by it.

LayoutPane.description: Stored pane (response object). Panes have no id of their own: they are addressed by `slot_index` and replaced as a set. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

chart_template_id.description: Chart template reference. Every non-null value is refused (`422` rule `chart_template_not_found`) until `chart_templates` ships; then it must name a template the caller may use.

indicator_preset_ids.description: Indicator preset references; omitted means `[]`. A non-empty list is refused (`422` rule `indicator_preset_not_found`) until panes resolve preset references; the preset store alone (E13-T03) does not lift this. Then every id must name a preset the caller may use.

interval_code.description: Bar series of a market pane; `null` for panes without one.

symbol.description: Bound symbol, market panes only: a Bybit USDT linear perpetual symbol of at most 20 characters (the DB `symbol_code` domain). It is not checked against the instrument catalogue. A non-null symbol on a live layout counts as chart-open for auto-recording.

LayoutPreset.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3); the embedded `layout` is a closed `LayoutInput`.

id.description: Stable for the life of the catalogue entry.

is_builtin.description: Always `true`: the catalogue is static. User-saved presets are layouts with a `hotkey_slot`.

OrderEntryRefusalReason.description: Why the shared order-entry gate refused an order (#837 Q5; E42-T03 and E27-T04). The server's set is closed and listed in `24-internal-schemas.md` 8.10. **Open-ended for readers:** clients must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a reason is an additive change (C-6.3).

count.description: Items in this page (not the total, which is never computed for unbounded sets).

total.description: Present only where a cheap exact count exists.

PaneConfig.description:
Per-pane view state with no column of its own, so a pane cannot become a blob store: closed
(unknown keys are refused, C-6.3; later stories add keys additively), at most 4096 bytes of
canonical compact UTF-8 JSON measured after sanitising (`422` rule `pane_config_too_large`),
and never holds credentials, account ids or user ids. Omitted means `{}`.

settings.description: Kind-specific flat settings (for example DOM depth, tape filters, CVD anchor, visible range), at most 32 keys. Every key must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$` (`422` rule `invalid_setting_key`); the server enforces this because generators cannot express key patterns. Numbers keep their kind (`1` stays `1`, `1.0` stays `1.0`). Omitted means `{}`.

sync_group.description: Cross-pane sync group (SCR-023); `null` or omitted means not synced. The axis defaults live on the layout (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`).

PaneIntervalCode.description: `<bar_type>:<param>`, exactly the `bar_type` and `param` of `/market/bars` (and of the WS topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`): `param` at most 24 characters, no leading zeros, and no trailing zeros in a `volume`/`delta` fraction, so each value has one spelling (`volume:0.5`, never `volume:0.50`), e.g. `time:1`, `time:D`, `tick:500`, `volume:0.5`, `renko:atr:14`, `pnf:10:3`. A `volume` or `delta` threshold must also be greater than 0 (`422` rule `interval_not_positive`).

PaneKind.description:
Pane kind (`lp_kind`, `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1). **Open-ended for readers:** clients
must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a kind is an additive change (C-6.3);
writers must send a listed value. Market panes (`chart`, `dom`, `tape`, `profile`, `cvd`,
`oi`, `deep_stats`, `regime`) may bind a `symbol` and `interval_code`; account panes
(`positions`, `journal`, `watchlist`, `alerts`) show many symbols and carry neither (rule
`property_not_allowed_for_kind`). `scanner` (SCR-104) also shows many symbols and carries
neither, but holds no account data: its rows are `runScanner`'s public market values;
E08-T09 PR 2a (`0054_scanner_presets`) added it to `lp_kind`. A heatmap lives in the
`dom` pane and orders in the `positions` pane. A footprint is a `chart` pane; until chart
templates exist (#2411) it is marked by `pane_config.settings.footprint: true`, its
options as further flat `footprint_*` settings.

PaneSettingValue.description: A flat setting value: a string, an integer or other finite number (each keeps its kind), a boolean, `null`, or an array of at most 32 such strings, numbers or booleans; objects are not allowed. Strings, also inside arrays, are at most 256 characters as sent and are then sanitised like `WorkspaceInput.name` (the name strip set and trimming), except that an empty result is kept; a lone surrogate is rule `invalid_unicode`. Numbers, also inside arrays, lie within ±1e15, so they read back with the same kind and value. A non-zero number must have |x| ≥ 1e-15 (`number_out_of_range`); zero is allowed. `-0.0` is stored as `0.0`.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem detail. `code` mirrors the `x-error-codes` catalogue.

action_class.description: `step_up_required` only: the step-up class the refused request needs, one of the `action_class` values of `POST /auth/step-up`.

action_summary.description: `step_up_required` only: server-composed text naming exactly what the refused request would execute, built from the validated request (for example "Release kill switch, scope global"). It comes from a fixed per-route template. Request values appear in it only as validated enum values (bare) or as identifiers and server-resolved labels (quoted, each bounded by its own schema's `maxLength` or `format`), never as free text such as a `reason`, and never as key material, a password, a token, a TOTP or recovery code or any field the redaction deny-list names (C-12.6). A label alone never identifies an account or a rule, because labels can be renamed and need not be unique: each account named in it is followed by its `environment` and `exchange_uid` and each rule by the environments its scope includes, rendered bare (for example "Release kill switch, accounts 'demo-1' (demo, UID 1001234)" or "Arm rule 'Break-even' (live)"); an account's `environment` and `exchange_uid` never change after it is registered. Naming a rule this way is provisional: two rules can share a label and environments, and `rules:write` can rename a rule and change its scope and its active version without a step-up, so the route slice of #2304 decides, before any rule template ships, whether a rule is also named by its bound accounts and whether the grant that arms it is also bound to its active version. Before a label is quoted, an apostrophe or a backslash in it is preceded by a backslash, and every character outside printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E) is written as `\u{`, its code point in upper-case hex zero-padded to four digits, and `}` (U+000A becomes `\u{000A}`, U+202E becomes `\u{202E}` and U+1F600 becomes `\u{1F600}`). That covers line breaks and other control characters, bidi embedding, override and isolate marks and look-alike quotation marks, so the quotes bound the label: the label `demo-1' (demo)` is quoted as `'demo-1\' (demo)'`. The step-up dialog shows it verbatim as its accessible description; a client never composes its own.

challenge_expires_at.description: `step_up_required` only: when the challenge expires, 5 minutes after issue (server clock). The client drops the held request then, without sending it.

challenge_id.description: `step_up_required` only: the challenge this refusal issued (#2304), a random UUIDv4 scoped to the issuing session, so a value from another session is unknown. One challenge is live per session; a newer refusal supersedes it. Send it as `challenge_id` to `POST /auth/step-up`, which requires it while the challenge is live, whatever the class; a step-up for a no-grace class must send it.

limit.description: The limit the value breaks, in the member's own unit.

symbol.description: The instrument whose exchange limit the value breaks, for a rule that checks one.

exchange.description: Present when the failure originated at Bybit.

failures_remaining.description: `mfa_invalid` from `POST /auth/step-up` only: how many more step-up attempts this session has before a failure downgrades it to read-only, 2 after its first consecutive failure and 1 after its second; the next failure is the third and answers `403 session_read_only` instead, without this member. It counts this session's own consecutive step-up failures only, the count stored on its session row: never another session's, never the account's sign-in lockout counter, so it reveals nothing beyond what this session has itself been told. A successful step-up starts the count again. Optional, additive (C-6.3).

idle_locked_at.description: `session_idle_locked` only: the session's `idle_deadline`, which is when it idle-locked, unless `POST /auth/lock` locked it first (the lock moment is then the `auth.session_locked` audit row's time), so it may be later than `server_time`. Read the problem code or `session.locked`, never this time, to tell that a session is locked.

instance.description: Correlation id, `urn:cv:req:{uuid}`; matches the `X-Correlation-Id` header and the audit entry.

recording_started_at.description: `no_data_recorded` from `GET /market/bars` only: when recording of the symbol's trade tape began, so the client can offer the first recorded window; null when nothing was ever recorded for the symbol. Optional, additive (C-6.3).

revoked_reason.description: `session_revoked` only. `expired`: the 12 h absolute lifetime elapsed. `unlock_attempts_exceeded`: five consecutive wrong unlock passwords. `revoked`: any other revocation; the specific cause is not disclosed.

step_up_reason.description: `step_up_required` only: the server-composed sentence saying why this action needs a fresh step-up, the line the step-up dialog (SCR-006, E09-D06) shows under the action, shown verbatim; the client adds no prefix and never composes its own. Present only when `action_class` is `live_enablement` or `killswitch`, carrying SCR-006's no-grace sentence verbatim: "Live enablement and kill-switch disable always need a fresh code, even right after a recent step-up." Omitted for every other class. Fixed text, never built from the request, so it carries no request value, label or credential material. Optional, additive (C-6.3).

target.description: `step_up_required` only: the exact, case-sensitive text a typed confirmation must equal when the action asks for one (for example the account name), else null. Like `action_summary`, it is an identifier or a server-resolved label of the validated request, never free text or credential material. It is a label only when no other object of its kind that the caller can see has that label, compared case-insensitively, and the label is printable ASCII; otherwise it is the object's identifier.

ProfileRiskCaps.description: Server-enforced caps, one gate each (SR-052, SR-053); `null` is no cap. A trading-enabled profile bounds every one (decision D11, `cap_unbounded`): `max_open_positions`, `max_concurrent_orders`, `max_leverage_cap`, and one cap of each pair, position size and daily loss.

max_daily_loss_pct.description: Percent of equity lost in a day, at least 0.1 and at most 50 (SCR-131).

max_daily_loss_usd.description: USDT lost in a day, above 0.

max_leverage_cap.description: At least 1, at most 100, and at least `leverage`.

max_position_pct_equity.description: Percent of equity, above 0 and at most 100.

ProfileSizing.description: Exactly the amount of `mode` is set and the others are absent or `null`: `qty` (`fixed_qty`), `notional_usd` (`fixed_notional`), `pct` (`pct_equity`), and one of `risk_per_trade_pct` and `risk_per_trade_usd` (`risk_based`).

min_leg_notional_usd.description: A leg below this notional, in USDT, is skipped rather than rejected; at least 0.

pct.description: Percent of equity per order, above 0 and at most 100.

risk_per_trade_pct.description: Percent of equity lost at the stop, above 0 and at most 100.

risk_per_trade_usd.description: USDT lost at the stop, above 0.

ProfileSizingMode.description: A profile's sizing mode, the Postgres type `sizing_mode` exactly: a profile never holds `SizingMode`'s request-time values `pct_position` and `profile`.

ProfileStopLoss.description: The native stop every order carries (C-2.6): `value` in `ticks` or `percent` of the reference price, or `atr_multiple` times ATR(`atr_period`), with `fallback_pct` while the ATR is unavailable. The member `unit` uses is required; the others take their defaults when left out and are kept for a later change of unit.

atr_multiple.description: The multiple of the ATR, above 0.

fallback_pct.description: The stop while the ATR is unavailable, in percent, above 0 and below 100.

value.description: The distance, above 0, in whole ticks or in percent (1.5 is 1.5 %).

ProfileStopUnit.description: A profile stop's unit: `offset_unit` without `r_multiple` (`ap_sl_unit`), because the stop defines R (24-internal-schemas.md section 9.3.1), and never `price`.

ProfileSymbolPattern.description: A listed USDT linear perpetual (`BTCUSDT`), or an anchored suffix pattern (`*USDT`) that is stored as written and matched against the listed, trading linear USDT perpetuals each time it is evaluated (SR-E28-06). A bare `*` is refused.

value.description: The distance, above 0, in `unit`; `r_multiple` is a multiple of the stop distance.

qty_pct.description: Percent of the leg's filled size, above 0 and at most 100.

r.description: The target, in R multiples of the stop distance, above 0.

ProfileTargetUnit.description: A profile take-profit's unit, the Postgres type `offset_unit` exactly; never `price`.

ProfileWarning.description: Advice that never blocks a save (SCR-130's `(!)` marker). A write's answer carries every warning; a read recomputes only `all_symbols` and `no_symbols`, which need no exchange data.

code.description: `all_symbols`: every listed symbol is allowed, by the flag or by the pattern `*USDT`; a write, which reads the instrument list, also flags an allow-list whose entries together match every listed symbol. Consider restricting. `no_symbols`: no symbol is allowed, so the profile sizes nothing (decision D11): an empty `allowed_symbols` without `all_symbols`, or the pattern `*USDT` in `blocked_symbols`; a write also flags a profile that allows none of the listed symbols. `sizing_below_min_order`: at the account's current equity the sizing gives less than `symbol`'s minimum order, and `message` works the example. `stop_beyond_liquidation`: the stop lies beyond the estimated liquidation distance at `leverage` (SR-E28-26). Open-ended for readers: a client shows a code it does not know by its `message` (C-6.3).

field.description: The JSON path of the member it is about.

ScannerClassSet.description: Matches a row whose class is any of `classes`, each one `listScannerCriteria` lists for the criterion (`422` rule `unknown_regime_class`); an empty set is `422` rule `classes_empty`.

ScannerCriterionId.description: A criterion id. `ScannerFilter` lists the ids in force; a stored preset may still name one the server no longer knows or lists with `available: false` (`ScannerPreset.unavailable_criteria`, which also carries a stored `sort` key that `sort_keys` lists with `available: false`).

ScannerFilter.description:
A closed set of criteria, each optional and applied together (AND); `{}` filters
nothing. Bounds are `Decimal` strings in the unit `listScannerCriteria` gives, both
inclusive; `min` must be below `max` (`422` rule `range_inverted`). A key outside the
set is `422` rule `unknown_criterion`, and a key `listScannerCriteria` lists with
`available: false` is `422` rule `criterion_unavailable`. Criteria with
`needs_recording: true` are
skipped for `live_only` rows (`runScanner`). Adding a criterion is additive; removing
one makes stored presets that name it report it in `unavailable_criteria`.

ScannerPreset.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

filter.description: The stored criteria the server knows today.

unavailable_criteria.description: Criteria the stored filter names that the server no longer knows or lists with `available: false`, never silently dropped (and the stored `sort` key when `sort_keys` lists it with `available: false`; `sort` is returned as stored): they are left out of `filter` and `runScanner`, and listed here until a `PUT` saves the preset without them. Usually empty.

version.description: 1 on create, raised by one on every change; informative only (no `If-Match`).

ScannerPresetInput.description:
Writable preset fields. `PUT` is a full replacement: an omitted field takes its default.
Only the server sets `id`, the owner (the caller), `version`, `unavailable_criteria`,
`created_at` and `updated_at`: sent in a body, each is refused (`422`) like any other
unknown property. `name` is at most 80 characters as sent (rule `string_too_long`),
then sanitised as `WorkspaceInput.name` is; empty after sanitising is rule
`string_too_short`, and a lone surrogate is rule `invalid_unicode`. `filter` is at most
4 KiB as stored JSON (rule `filter_too_large`). A preset never stores results.

is_default.description: The preset a new scanner pane opens with. At most one per owner: setting it clears the owner's previous default (`createScannerPreset`).

name.description: At most 80 characters as sent, at least 1 after sanitising (above). Unique per owner, case-insensitive (`409 conflict`, rule `name_taken`).

sort.description: The ranking the preset applies; omitted means `turnover_24h`.

ScannerRange.description: An inclusive range: at least one bound (`422` rule `range_empty`), and `min` below `max` when both are given (`422` rule `range_inverted` for `min >= max`).

ScannerSortKey.description: A `runScanner` ranking key. **Open-ended for readers** (C-6.3); a writer sends a listed value that `listScannerCriteria`'s `sort_keys` does not list with `available: false`. A preset stores one.

Symbol.description: Bybit USDT linear perpetual symbol. v1 accepts USDT-quoted linear symbols only.

TradingDisabledProblem.description: The `403 trading_disabled` problem the order-entry gate returns when it refuses a submission or amend that opens or increases exposure, before any OMS work (C-2.21): the problem body plus the gate's `reason`. `detail` is human text and never carries an id or a secret. The gate runs after authentication, RBAC and account-scope resolution, so an account outside the caller's scope never reaches it: an id route answers it as a missing id (`404`), and a request that names it in its body is refused with `403 account_scope_denied` (SR-E29-13). Cancels, flatten and quantity-reducing or stop-tightening amends never pass through the gate. Attaching a missing native SL, tightening a stop, or re-arming a protective trigger is never gated; "trigger re-armed" means an exposure-increasing (entry) trigger. An amend with any risk-increasing component is gated.

Watchlist.description: One of the caller's lists as stored: the members of `WatchlistInput`, under the same rules, and the server's own. Every member is always answered (`columns` empty when none is chosen). Closed on purpose: a list's members are exactly these.

version.description: Server-assigned: 1 on create, one more on each replace. `updateWatchlist` takes it back through `If-Match` (`WatchlistETag`), never in the body.

columns.description: Column ids shown for this watchlist, in order: the ids of E08-D07 §4.1 (`last`, `chg_24h_pct`, `open_interest_value`, ...). Ids are stored strings and a reader skips one it does not know (E08-D07 D8), so the set is open: at most 32, each a lowercase snake_case id of at most 32 characters, none twice (`422 validation_failed` on `columns`, rule `duplicate_column`). Left out or `null`, on a create and on a replace alike, the list takes E08-D07 §4.1's default columns (`symbol`, `last`, `chg_24h_pct`, `turnover_24h`, `funding_rate`, `next_funding`, `oi_chg_24h_pct`, `spread_bps`, `rec`): a replace without `columns` resets them, as a full replace does.

name.description: Trimmed of leading and trailing white space before it is checked and stored: E08-D07 §4.3 and DJ compare names trimmed and case-insensitively; the 1–80 characters count the trimmed name, so a name blank once trimmed is `422 validation_failed`. A name holding a control or format character (Unicode Cc or Cf) is `422 validation_failed`, as an account-profile name is. Unique among the owner's lists, case-insensitively as Postgres `lower()` folds it (`409 conflict` / `name_taken`).

symbols.description: The list, in order: each a trading USDT linear perpetual of the instrument catalogue, none twice (`422 validation_failed`: `too_many_symbols`, `unknown_symbol`, `duplicate_symbol`).

Workspace.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

updated_at.description: Concurrency token (also the `ETag`) for the workspace metadata only; layout writes do not change it. Always exactly 6 fractional digits plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`) and strictly increasing on every write. Echo it exactly as received; never re-serialise it through a client date type.

WorkspaceBundle.description: Portable, credential-free export of presentation state only.

indicator_presets.description: Export holds only the caller's live presets, never a built-in or another user's: at most 500, the per-user cap of `createIndicatorPreset`, and never truncated to the import limits below. Import (E15-S07; no operation takes a bundle yet) never trusts them: every item is validated again as on `createIndicatorPreset`, so `is_builtin` and `owner_user_id` are never honoured (an item carrying either is refused), the importer owns what is imported, and the array is imported whole or not at all. The server refuses it whole beyond 200 items or 1 MiB of preset JSON (SR-E13-07's import limits; the 1 MiB counts this array, not the whole bundle), on any invalid item, or when it would take the importer past 500 live presets.

WorkspaceDetail.description: Response object: `Workspace` plus every live layout with its panes, so restore is one request per workspace. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

WorkspaceIconToken.description:
Design-system icon token for the workspace (a token name, never a URL or markup).
**Open-ended for readers:** clients must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a token
is an additive change (C-6.3). Writers must send a listed value; the server keeps the same
allow-list. `workspace.default` is the only token until the design-system icon registry
(CMP-019) publishes workspace icons.

WorkspaceInput.description:
Writable workspace fields. `PUT` is a full replacement: an omitted field takes its default,
and an explicit `null` is refused (`422`).

Observable validation (all `422 validation_failed`): JSON nesting depth must be at most 16;
`NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected; a string that cannot be encoded as UTF-8 (a lone
surrogate) is rule `invalid_unicode`. `name` is at most 40 characters as sent (rule
`string_too_long`), then sanitised: U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F, U+2028, U+2029, U+061C,
U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 are removed, then surrounding whitespace is
trimmed; nothing else is altered. Empty after sanitising is rule `string_too_short`. Reads
return the sanitised name.

is_default.description: At most one live default per user; `true` clears the previous default in the same transaction.

post.description:
The server mints a UUIDv7 `id`. The body is limited to 64 KiB (`413 payload_too_large`).
A non-null `layout_id` must name one of the caller's live layouts, otherwise
`422` rule `layout_not_found` (every non-null value until layouts ship, E15-T01).
The `ETag` response header carries the `updated_at` token for later `If-Match` use.

`Idempotency-Key`: the same key with the same body replays the stored 2xx response with
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.
Replay storage is best-effort and bounded; correctness never depends on it.
The replay cache is in memory and bounded: a retry after the entry was evicted, or after a
server restart, creates a **duplicate** drawing. Clients that need retry-safe creation
should use `batchUpsertDrawings` with a client-chosen `id` (a repeat is `409 id_unavailable`).

The chart engine batches drawing mutations during a drag with a 500 ms debounce, so a single
call carries all affected shapes.

Processing order: (1) the body is limited to 1 MiB and `operations` to 200 items, otherwise
`413 payload_too_large`, checked before per-operation validation; (2) the whole body is
validated (`422`, up to 20 field errors such as `operations.3.drawing.tool`; each `id` may
appear at most once per batch, else rule `duplicate_id`); (3) the operations are applied in
order inside **one transaction**. The first operation that cannot be applied rolls the
whole batch back and returns `409 conflict` with `errors[0] = {field: "operations.<i>", rule, message}`,
where `rule` is one of:

- `target_unavailable` — an `update`/`delete` target is missing, soft-deleted or owned by
  another user (indistinguishable by design);
- `version_conflict` — the operation's `if_match` is stale;
- `id_unavailable` — a `create` id is already used by any row of any owner in any state
  (an id stays unavailable until its row is purged, 90 days after deletion; re-create under a new id).

`create.id` is optional (client UUIDv7 recommended); `update` and `delete` require `if_match`,
the `updated_at` token of the version being replaced or removed. The result lists the
created, updated and deleted ids in operation order.

`Idempotency-Key` behaves as on `createDrawing`.

put.description:
Owner only, after a step-up for class `risk_caps`, as `createAccountProfile`. The one
operation that moves the account's default (decision D7): the body names the profile to
bind and nothing else. A `profile_id` that is missing, deleted or another account's is
`404`, as an account outside the caller's grants is, and so is an account of another
environment than this server's (C-2.11), and a body that fails its schema is
`422 validation_failed`, and one over 1 KiB `413 payload_too_large`; none is audited.

`If-Match` is required and takes this binding's `ETag`, never a profile's, and it is
checked before the profile the body names. Without it the answer is
`428 precondition_required`; a stale one is `412 version_conflict`, even when the default
has since come back to the profile it was on, because the tag names the binding's
version. Either way nothing changes: reload, then move again. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` and body is answered from the stored `200` before `If-Match` is read,
so a move whose answer was lost is not refused, but only once the session holds the
`risk_caps` step-up: a retry without one is challenged (`403 step_up_required`) before the
stored answer is served; the key with another body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A first send's stale `If-Match` (`412`) or missing profile
(`404`) is refused before the step-up, never challenged.

The move is audited write-ahead in its transaction, as `profile.unbound` for the default
it replaces, then `profile.bound` for the new one: when either record cannot be written
nothing changes (`503 audit_unavailable`). The server judges the move cap by cap over
`ProfileRiskCaps`: `null` is no bound, and every cap of a profile that cannot trade
(`enabled` or `trading_enabled` false) counts as zero, since it sizes nothing;
`allowed_symbols` is not compared. When any cap is higher on the new default than on the
one it replaces, `profile.bound` is labelled `relaxing` and the Owner is notified
(SR-E28-01). So a move onto the bootstrap `Default` while it cannot trade is not relaxing,
even with `null` caps, and a move that turns trading on, from a default that cannot
trade, is always relaxing. Binding the profile that already is the default changes
nothing, writes no record and answers the binding with its current `ETag`.

Refused with `409 conflict`, nothing changed and `detail` naming each blocker, while the profile is the account's default (make another profile the default first, with `setAccountDefaultProfile`) or while any armed rule covers the account: one whose scope lists the account among its accounts, or lists no account (or an element that is not a readable account id) and so covers every account (a global rule), whatever its scope level, each named by its id and name (a rule cannot name a profile yet). `If-Match` is required: a delete needs the current `ETag`, and last-write-wins is refused on risk caps by contract. put.description:
Owner only, after a step-up for class `risk_caps`, as `createAccountProfile`. A PUT
replaces the whole profile: a member it leaves out takes its default, never the stored
value, so omitting `risk_caps` clears every cap and resets `max_orders_per_minute` to its
server default of 30; send the full object. It is checked as a create is, a `name` that
another profile of the account uses is `409 conflict`, and the profile is stored as its
next `version`; the previous version stays readable as a revision, and a position sized
from it keeps it. `require_native_stop` cannot be set to `false`: the attempt is
`422 validation_failed` / `native_stop_mandatory`, audited as `profile.save_refused`
(SR-E28-08). A body over 64 KiB is `413 payload_too_large`, as on a create.

A replace never moves the account's default: the default binding moves only through its
own operation (`setAccountDefaultProfile`). A body whose `is_default` differs from the
stored one (left out, it is `false`) is `422 validation_failed` /
`default_has_own_operation`; one that repeats it is accepted, so a profile read and sent
back whole is a valid replace.

`If-Match` is required: a replace needs the current `ETag`, and last-write-wins is refused
on risk caps by contract. Without it the answer is `428 precondition_required`; a stale
one is `412 version_conflict`. Either way nothing changes: reload, then edit again.
Audited write-ahead as `profile.updated` with the profile before and after: when that
record cannot be written nothing changes (`503 audit_unavailable`). The server judges a
replace as it judges a move (`setAccountDefaultProfile`), cap by cap: `null` is no bound,
and every cap of a profile that cannot trade counts as zero. A replace that loosens a cap,
or widens what a profile that can trade allows (an allow entry added or changed,
`all_symbols` set, a block entry removed), is labelled `relaxing` in that record and
notifies the Owner (SR-E28-01). So turning trading off, or clearing the caps of a profile
that cannot trade, is never relaxing, and turning trading on always is.

get.description:
The built-in presets and the caller's live presets, never another user's, whatever the
caller's role. Built-ins come first, then by `indicator_code`, case-insensitive `name` and
`id`; deleted presets are not listed. A user holds at most 500 live presets, so the list is
not paged. Any query parameter is refused with `422` (SR-026).

post.description:
Saves a preset owned by the caller; the server mints its `id`. Built-ins never change:
customising one saves a copy with this call, checked like any other save, so the copy is
refused (`422` rule `unknown_indicator`) while `listIndicators` does not list the
built-in's indicator. Nothing is stored on any refusal.

- `413 payload_too_large`: the body is over 16 KiB, refused before it is parsed.
- `422 validation_failed` (`IndicatorPresetInput` gives each field's rules): an unknown
  property (`is_builtin`, `owner_user_id` and `id` included), `invalid_indicator_code`,
  `unknown_indicator`, a `params` keyword (`type`, `enum`, `minimum`, `maximum` or
  `multipleOf` on `params.<name>`, `additionalProperties` on `params`),
  `params_too_large`, `params_too_deep`, `params_too_many_keys`, `style_not_allowed`,
  the `name` rules and `invalid_unicode`. Any query parameter is refused (SR-026).
- `409 conflict`: rule `name_taken` (the caller has a live preset with this
  `indicator_code` and name, case-insensitive) or `limit_reached` (500 live presets).
- `503`: `store_unavailable` when storage fails, `audit_unavailable` when the write-ahead
  audit record cannot be written.

delete.description:
Soft delete, never a hard delete: the preset leaves the list and its name can be used
again, while the row is kept with `deleted_at` set. No precondition. A preset that is
missing, already deleted or another user's returns the same `404`; a built-in is `403`
rule `builtin_immutable`, as on `updateIndicatorPreset`. A malformed `presetId` is `422`
rule `uuid_parsing`, and any query parameter is refused (SR-026). `503` as on
`createIndicatorPreset`.

put.description:
Full replacement of one of the caller's presets (an omitted field takes its default). No
precondition: the last write wins. A preset that is missing, deleted or another user's
returns the same `404`. A built-in is `403 forbidden` with rule `builtin_immutable` (a
missing permission is the usual `403` with `required_permissions`). `indicator_code` is
immutable (`422` rule `immutable_field`), and a malformed `presetId` is `422` rule
`uuid_parsing`. `409`, `413`, the other `422` rules and `503` as on
`createIndicatorPreset`.

Evaluation order for `/indicator-presets*` (steps that do not apply are skipped): `401`;
`403` (permission, CSRF); `413`; `422` (path, query, body, none of which reads a stored
preset); `404` (missing, deleted or another user's, identical); `403` rule
`builtin_immutable`; `422` rule `immutable_field`; `409`; the write. `503` wherever
storage or the write-ahead audit record fails.

get.description:
Static built-in catalogue served from the code (no rows, nothing user-scoped). Each entry
carries a complete `LayoutInput` for `createLayout`, symbols left for the client to fill

(`listLayouts`). Ids are stable and new entries are additive. Thumbnails are static client

get.description:
The caller's presets, never another user's, whatever the caller's role, ordered by
case-insensitive `name` then `id`. A preset holds criteria and a ranking, never results.
A user holds at most 100 presets, so the list is not paged. Any query parameter is
refused with `422` (SR-026).

post.description:
Saves a preset owned by the caller; the server mints its `id` and sets `version` to 1.
Its `filter` is checked against the current criteria as `runScanner` checks `filters`.
Nothing is stored on any refusal.

- `413 payload_too_large`: the body is over 8 KiB, refused before it is parsed.
- `422 validation_failed` (`ScannerPresetInput` gives each field's rules): an unknown
  property (`id`, `version`, `unavailable_criteria` and the timestamps included), the
  `name` rules and `invalid_unicode`, an unknown `sort`, `runScanner`'s filter rules
  with `errors[].field` `filter.<criterion id>` (else `filter`), and
  `criterion_unavailable` on `filter.<criterion id>` or `sort`, as `runScanner` refuses
  them. Any query parameter is refused (SR-026).
- `409 conflict`: rule `name_taken` (the caller has a preset with this name,
  case-insensitive), `limit_reached` (100 presets) or `conflict` (a concurrent default
  that still trips the one-default index after one retry).
- `503`: `store_unavailable` when storage fails, `audit_unavailable` when the write-ahead
  audit record cannot be written.

`is_default: true` makes this the caller's one default preset: in the same transaction
the server clears the flag on the caller's previous default, a change recorded as that
preset's `scanner_preset.updated` with its `version` raised.

delete.description:
Hard delete: the row goes and its name can be used again at once; the write-ahead
`scanner_preset.deleted` record keeps its content hash. Deleting the default leaves the
caller with none. No precondition. A preset that is missing, already deleted or another
user's returns the same `404`; a malformed `presetId` is `422` rule `uuid_parsing`, and
any query parameter is refused (SR-026). `503` as on `createScannerPreset`.

put.description:
Full replacement of one of the caller's presets (an omitted field takes its default);
the server raises `version` by one. No precondition: the last write wins. A preset that
is missing, deleted or another user's returns the same `404`. A malformed `presetId` is
`422` rule `uuid_parsing`. `is_default`, `409`, `413`, the other `422` rules and `503`
as on `createScannerPreset`. Saving a preset whose stored filter names an unavailable
criterion stores the body's `filter` only, so the criterion is dropped by that save and
no other way.

`403` (permission, CSRF); `413`; `422` (path, query, body, none of which reads a stored
preset); `404` (missing, deleted or another user's, identical); `409`; the write. `503`
wherever storage or the write-ahead audit record fails.

post.description: Creates one of the caller's lists at `version` 1 (E08-T07). A `name` that another of the caller's lists already uses, case-insensitively (as Postgres `lower()` folds it), is `409 conflict` with `errors[0].rule = name_taken` and `field` `name`. A list that breaks a rule of `WatchlistInput` is `422 validation_failed` naming the field and the rule: `too_many_symbols` (over 200), `unknown_symbol` (not a trading USDT linear perpetual of the instrument catalogue) or `duplicate_symbol` (a symbol twice in one list), each on `symbols`. Either way nothing is written. A body over 64 KiB is `413 payload_too_large`, and while the instrument catalogue is not loaded a list that holds a symbol is `503 instrument_cache_unavailable` (`WatchlistSaveUnavailable`). A list with no symbols needs no catalogue, so it is never `503 instrument_cache_unavailable`. When several refusals apply, the first in this order answers: `413`, then `422` for the rules that need no catalogue (`name`, `columns`, `too_many_symbols`, `duplicate_symbol`), then `503 instrument_cache_unavailable`, then `422` for `unknown_symbol`, then `409`. put.description: Replaces the whole list and stores it as its next `version` (E08-T07). `If-Match` is required: a stale write is never applied silently. Without it the answer is `428 precondition_required`; with a tag that does not name the list's current version the answer is `412 version_conflict`, whose `ETag` header names the current version. 422.description: Semantically invalid layout. `code: validation_failed`; each entry of `errors[]` names the offending field, a pane by its array position.

get.description:
The layout with all of its panes (by `slot_index`). It must be live and belong to the named
workspace, one of the caller's live workspaces; otherwise the same `404`. The `ETag` header
carries the `updated_at` token.

put.description:
Called on pane rearrangement with a 2-second debounce. `If-Match` prevents a stale tab from
clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window.

Full replacement of the layout **and its whole pane set** in one transaction, validated as
on `createLayout` before anything is written; partial application is impossible. The
`updated_at` token versions the aggregate, so a pane-only change also changes it.
`If-Match`, the no-op rule and `412 version_conflict` work as on `updateWorkspace`; after a
`412` the stored layout is unchanged and the client re-reads it with `getLayout`. `404` as
on `getLayout`; `409`, `422` and the 128 KiB limit as on `createLayout`.
